0.value:
Loads every .pt file in a folder into a torch Dataset, for training code - it has no inlets and no outlets.

Give it a folder as its argument. Each .pt file there (a tensor saved with torch.save) is loaded and kept under its file name, and the node holds the result as a torch Dataset: item i is a dictionary of the i-th row of every file, and the length is the shortest file's length.

NOTHING IN A PATCH CAN READ IT:
The node exposes no inlets and no outlets, so a patch cannot ask it for anything. It is groundwork for training code that reaches the node from Python, not a way to bring data into a patch. To get recorded data into a patch use np.load (a NumPy file) or np.sequence (a recording); to make test tensors, t.rand or t.linspace.

SYNTAX:
t.data_set <folder>
With no folder, nothing is loaded.

EXAMPLE:
t.data_set /Users/me/datasets/poses

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:
The folder, as the argument. It is read once, when the node is made. A folder that does not exist prints a message in the console and leaves the dataset empty; a .pt file that cannot be read is skipped with a message and the rest are kept.

OUTPUTS:
None.

RELATED:
np.load reads a saved NumPy array into a patch. t.buffer and t.rolling_buffer collect data as it arrives.
